source.original_title: 05/12/2026 - Greg Fontenot & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/12/2026 - Greg Fontenot & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

prospect.name: Abraham
prospect.location: Catalonia, Spain — rural area on a radio internet connection
prospect.occupation: Forklift operator; the machine carries most weight but he has to lift heavy boxes by hand at times
prospect.family_status: Not established. Has two dogs. No partner or children were ever asked about or mentioned.
prospect.training_background: No fitness background until roughly two years ago, when he started going to the gym and built what he calls a pretty nice physique for his expectations. About a year in he developed elbow and shoulder pain, and the last year has been much lighter training. Now cannot bench press or do bicep curls and avoids exercises. Trained four or five days a week at his peak. Owns 6 kg and 12 kg kettlebells and saves Trevor's reels. Holds a Skool subscription for acroyoga.
prospect.medical: Elbow and shoulder pain that began roughly a year into strength training and has persisted about a year. Prevents bench pressing and bicep curls, interferes with lifting boxes at work, and causes him to avoid jumping and dropping from height. No diagnosis, imaging or treating clinician was mentioned, because no question was asked about any of it.

signals: Lost a year of progress and the identity that came with it to an injury — 'I was happy with a new way of life, about working out, maybe four or five days a week. And that was fulfilling me. And now, I don't feel the same... I don't feel good now. I don't want to go to the gym.'
Wants to resume rather than start — 'I would like to bench press again. I cannot bench press anymore'

Overlaps with the_medically_constrained: high intent and blocked by an injury. Assigned rebuilder instead because the definition requires no price resistance, and price was an absolute barrier here — he could not afford even the $200 product this month.

Overlaps with the_optimizer on ambition: he already has the physique and wants capability beyond it — 'I look good. Only that. And I want something more' — but has none of the optimizer's financial profile

goals.text: Train hard without getting injured again — 'not get injured by, with, with training, with hard training, with strength training'
A body capable of doing whatever he wants — more explosive, more flexible, better endurance
Walk in the mountains for more than one or two hours without getting tired
Keep up with his two dogs, and with friends at Airsoft who climb walls and drop one to two metres
Lift heavy boxes at work without the elbow failing him
Return to pressing and curling in some form — 'I want to be able to do that in a different way, but I want to keep going'
Regain flexibility lost over two years of gym training
Not slide back to who he was two years ago — 'only sitting on the sofa and doing nothing, getting a big, big fat belly'

pains.text: Elbow and shoulder pain for roughly a year, preventing bench press and bicep curls and forcing him to avoid exercises
Lost the fulfilment training gave him — 'that was fulfilling me. And now, I don't feel the same about this kind of workout... I don't want to go to the gym'
Does not know how to fix it — 'Well, I just want... How to fix that, and I don't know how'
Cannot follow his friends at Airsoft because of endurance and agility, and avoids jumping for fear of injury — 'if I do that, I will get hurt'
Embarrassment at work when he cannot lift boxes that female colleagues are carrying — 'I go with my, I think, not bad physique, and I pick up the box, and I'm, oh no, I can't do that. It's not good'
Two years of gym training left him strong-looking but inflexible — 'I'm not so flexible. And it's just, I look good. Only that'
Fear of regressing to a sedentary life if he does not act now
Severe financial constraint — could not afford any coaching tier and could not afford the $200 product until the middle of the following month

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, it's about me, not about your thing. It's about me. What are some of the concerns or hesitations that you have on your side? It's my financials with my money. I don't have much more money.
objections.rep_response: Deferred it rather than working it — 'We have so many different programs to accommodate for people who... don't have that much money. Don't worry about that for now. I just want to make sure that you're confident in the plan.' Correct instinct to isolate belief first, but he never returned to build a financial picture.

objections.raw_quote: I will be able to do any of them, but with my situation, with my financial situation, I will only can... Afford the university.
objections.rep_response: Accepted immediately and screen-shared Primal University without probing cash, credit or capacity at all

objections.raw_quote: This month, I cannot. Okay. have to wait the next maybe.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed the reason was money only, declined to press ('I'm not going to judge you for that'), pinned a date for mid-June, and committed to two follow-up contacts. Directed him to free YouTube and Instagram content in the meantime.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Primal University offered at $200/month, presented as effectively a single $200 purchase on the basis that it can be cancelled after one month.

evidence: Declined both coaching tiers on affordability: 'with my financial situation, I will only can... Afford the university.'
Wanted the $200 product but could not pay this month — 'This month, I cannot. I have to wait the next maybe' — and named mid-June
Two concrete follow-ups committed by the rep: an assistant contact at the end of May and a further contact around 15 June, with a note made on file
No payment link sent, no money collected, nothing signed

Counter-evidence on intent: belief was high once money was set aside — 'I'm super confident with your plan, what you explain me with the three pillars' and 'If I make a decision, if I go all in, I know it will work'
outcome.next_step: Assistant to contact at the end of May, rep to contact again around 15 June to enrol him in Primal University at $200. Meanwhile directed to free YouTube and Instagram content and told to use the 6 kg kettlebell rather than the 12 kg.

notable.note: Third mis-titled file in this batch. The title names Greg Fontenot and carries a KFS setter suffix; the call is entirely with a man named Abraham in rural Catalonia, and no setter is identifiable, so the KFS attribution cannot be trusted for this record. Two substantive problems on the call. First, a year-old unresolved elbow and shoulder injury that stops him pressing, curling and lifting at work was never assessed — the rep asked when it started and nothing else, then told him the programme would 'get rid of the injuries in your body', prescribed a specific load ('I'd stick to the 6 if 12 is a bit uncomfortable') and sent him to Instagram reels to 'alleviate some of these problems in your body'. Second, there is a direct contradiction on the record about his age: he answers 'I'm 59 this year', and ten minutes later the rep twice frames advice around him 'entering your forties in the next year' and 'as we enter our forties'. One of the two is wrong and the age in this record is not reliable. Pricing also deviated: $4,000 for three months was offered and the sanctioned $9,000 twelve-month tier was not mentioned at all. Notably, the one thing he explicitly asked for was technique correction, and the product he was steered to is the one without it.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, worsened by connection problems on a rural radio link and by the prospect being a non-native English speaker with frequent short turns. The rep's own questions repeatedly appear under the prospect's label — 'How old are you, Abraham?', 'What do you do for work?', 'What are some of the concerns or hesitations that you have on your side?' — with the answer following in the same block. Roles resolved from content. A direct factual contradiction sits in the transcript: the prospect states he is 59 this year, the rep twice says he is entering his forties. The prospect's surname is never spoken and is not recoverable, since the title belongs to a different person.
